findings.title: All success criteria traced to tasks
findings.description: Cross-reference: SC1–2 (enum + field) → Tasks 1.1–1.2; SC3–4 (loader, case-insensitive, missing-key default, ConfigError) → Task 1.3 with matching tests in 1.4; SC5 (round-trip) → `test_bounds_policy_yaml_round_trip` in 1.4; SC6 (OPEN no-op) → Task 2.3 OPEN tests + Task 3.4 `test_open_policy_does_not_call_enforcement` (the mock/spy option SC10 allows); SC7–8 (wrap semantics incl. multi-width and negative overshoot, velocities unchanged) → Task 2.3 wrap tests including `test_wrap_large_overshoot`, `test_wrap_negative_large_overshoot`, `test_wrap_edge_exact_upper`, `test_wrap_velocities_unchanged`; SC9 (reflect clamp + sign flip) → Task 2.3 reflect tests incl. idempotent-bounce case; SC10–11 (step wiring + 50-tick integration) → Tasks 3.2/3.4 with the exact three policy assertions; SC12 (both YAMLs use wrap) → Tasks 4.1–4.2; SC13 (full pytest) → Tasks 3.5/5.1; SC14 (manual viewer verification, all three modes) → Task 5.2 walkthrough steps 4–7 mirroring the slice's Verification Walkthrough. Out-of-scope items (SOFT policy, axis-mixed policies, engine changes) correctly absent.

findings.title: Sequencing and commit placement correct
findings.description: Each section is self-contained and independently completable: config enum/loader land and are tested before the enforcement module (which imports `BoundsPolicy`); enforcement module is tested before `SimulationManager` consumes it; the required `world_bounds` constructor parameter (Task 3.1) correctly includes Task 3.5 to sweep other call sites (`test_force_builder.py`, `test_clients.py`) rather than leaving that to chance. Commits at Tasks 1.5, 2.4, 3.6, 4.3, 5.5 each follow a green test run. Config-defaults tasks (Section 4) are placed after integration so the shipped YAMLs load with a fully tested code path.

findings.title: Task 2.2 pins implementation detail consistent with the slice design
findings.description: Task 2.2 dictates the exact numpy idiom (`np.mod(..., out=...)`, boolean-mask `np.abs`/`-np.abs` flips) rather than just the behavioral contract. This is acceptable here because the slice design's "Policy Semantics" section itself specifies these exact semantics (modulo handling of negative/multi-width overshoot, idempotent abs-based velocity flips) — the task is faithful to the parent, not adding unspecified detail. No action needed; flagged only so reviewers know this level of step detail is inherited, not invented.

findings.title: No load-test or CI task needed
findings.description: The slice design restates no NFR and no performance requirement beyond "negligible cost for the default path," which the OPEN-path gating and the mock test in Task 3.4 cover functionally. No `tests/load/` task is required, and none is missing.
